 The RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 October 2026, its first hike since February 2023 ( RBI policy statement ). Company fixed deposits moved within days: Bajaj Finance raised rates from 7 October and Shriram Finance from 11 October, by up to 40 bps.
 We track 9 NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs) that take public deposits. The highest rate right now is 9.10% from Muthoot Capital Services. The table below is updated every month and shows rates as on 9 Nov 2026.

 What the RBI Hike Means for Company FD Rates 
 NBFCs borrow from banks and the bond market, and both get costlier when the repo rate rises. Public deposits are another funding source, so NBFCs raise FD rates to attract more of them. The RBI also changed its stance to “calibrated tightening”, so near-term rate cuts are off the table.
 NBFCs usually pay 0.5–2% more than large banks because they carry higher credit risk, and their deposits have no DICGC insurance.

 What Stands Out in This Data 
 Rate leader: Muthoot Capital’s 9.10% (36 months) is about 1.25% above the next large NBFC. Its credit rating (CRISIL A+) is lower than the AAA-rated names.
 Rating vs rate: AAA-rated companies like Bajaj Finance, Sundaram Finance and LIC Housing pay 7.35–7.75% at their best tenure. The extra yield above that comes with extra credit risk.
 Tenure sweet spot: most NBFCs pay their highest rate at 3–5 years. One-year rates are 0.5–1% lower.
 Who moved: only Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance have announced post-hike revisions so far. The others may follow.
 Risks to Check Before Investing in a Company FD 
 Credit rating: prefer AAA or AA+ from CRISIL, ICRA, CARE or India Ratings. Check it again at renewal, since ratings can be cut.
 No deposit insurance: if the company defaults, nothing is insured. Spread larger amounts across companies.
 Premature withdrawal: within 3 months, you can withdraw up to 50% of the principal or ₹5 lakh (whichever is lower), without interest. Critical illness allows 100% withdrawal, and deposits up to ₹10,000 can be withdrawn in full ( Moneylife ). After 3 months, the company’s own penalty rules apply.
 Track record: check how long the company has been accepting public deposits and whether it has ever delayed repayments.
 Cumulative vs Non-Cumulative Payout 
 A cumulative FD reinvests the interest and pays everything at maturity. A non-cumulative FD pays interest monthly, quarterly or yearly, and those rates are slightly lower.
 Example: ₹1,00,000 for 3 years at 7.85%, assuming annual compounding.

 Cumulative suits investors who don’t need regular income. Non-cumulative suits retirees who need a regular payout.

 Taxation and TDS on Company FDs 
 FD interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.
 Companies deduct TDS at 10% once your interest from that company crosses ₹10,000 in a year (20% without PAN). The higher ₹50,000 / ₹1 lakh limits apply only to banks and post offices.
 From tax year 2026-27, Form 121 replaces Forms 15G/15H for TDS-free interest if your total income is below the taxable limit.
 Cumulative FDs still face TDS each year on the interest that accrues, even though you receive nothing until maturity.
 Will Company FD Rates Rise Further? 
 The next MPC meeting is on 2–4 December 2026. The RBI’s “calibrated tightening” stance keeps another hike possible but not certain. NBFC FD rates usually follow the policy rate with a lag of a few weeks. We will update the table after the December policy.
 FAQs 
 Are company FDs safe? 
 They carry more risk than bank FDs because they have no DICGC insurance. Safety depends mainly on the company’s credit rating and financial strength.
 Which NBFC pays the highest FD rate right now? 
 Muthoot Capital Services pays up to 9.10% as on 9 Nov 2026. Check the full table above for tenure-wise rates.
 Can I withdraw a company FD early? 
 Yes. Within 3 months, you can withdraw up to 50% of the principal or ₹5 lakh (whichever is lower), without interest. After 3 months, the company’s own penalty applies.
 Is TDS deducted on company FD interest? 
 Yes, at 10% if your interest from one company crosses ₹10,000 in a financial year.
 Do senior citizens get higher rates on company FDs? 
 Most NBFCs pay 0.25–0.50% extra to depositors aged 60 and above.
